facts.statement: The genus Machairoceratops contains only one known species, M. cronusi, which was first described and named in 2016.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, M. cronusi, first described and named in 2016 by Eric K. Lund, Patrick M. O'Connor, Mark A. Loewen, and Zubair A. Jinnah.

facts.statement: The animal is known only from the holotype specimen UMNH VP 20550, discovered in 2006 and now held at the Natural History Museum of Utah.
facts.quote: Machairoceratops is known solely from the holotype UMNH VP 20550, found in 2006, which is housed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

facts.statement: Its genus name means "bent sword" because of the two forward-curving horns located at the top of its frill.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek machairis, meaning "bent sword", in reference to its unique frill ornamentation showing two forward curving horns on the frill's uppermost part

facts.statement: The species name cronusi honors the Greek god Cronus, who is depicted in mythology carrying a curved sickle.
facts.quote: The specific name cronusi refers to Cronus, a Greek god who deposed his father Uranus by castrating him with a sickle or scythe based on the mythology, and as such is shown carrying a curved bladed weapon.

facts.statement: It was a four-legged herbivore that possessed a frill to protect its neck.
facts.quote: Machairoceratops was a quadrupedal herbivore with a frill protecting its neck.

facts.statement: The top of its skull featured a single pair of long, curved spikes that were 44 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The top of the parietal bone features only one pair of long, curved, anteroposteriorly oriented spikes measuring 44 cm in length.

facts.statement: Unlike other centrosaurines, the sides of its frill lacked smaller epiparietal bones.
facts.quote: The sides of the frill lack the smaller epiparietales that are present in other centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Its postorbital horns measured 27 centimeters in length, though their exact orientation on the skull is unknown.
facts.quote: The postorbital horns, measuring 27 cm in length, are detached from the skull, and their exact orientation is unknown.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is approximately the same size as the dinosaur Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: The holotype of Machairoceratops is very close in size or the same size as Diabloceratops.

facts.statement: This extinct centrosaurine dinosaur lived during the Late Cretaceous in the Wahweap Formation of southern Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Machairoceratops (meaning "bent sword horned face"), previously known as the "Wahweap centrosaurine B", is an extinct genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Wahweap Formation (late Campanian stage) of Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument, southern Utah, United States.

facts.statement: The precise age of the animal is estimated to be 80.06 million years ago, with an uncertainty range between 80.68 and 79.26 million years ago.
facts.quote: The precise age of Machairoceratops has been estimated to be 80.06 Ma, with a range of uncertainty between 80.68-79.26 Ma.

facts.statement: When it lived, the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest, nearly isolating southern Laramidia from the rest of North America.
facts.quote: During the time that Machairoceratops lived, the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest extent, almost completely isolating southern Laramidia from the rest of North America.

facts.statement: Its habitat included lakes, floodplains, and rivers flowing to the east.
facts.quote: The area where dinosaurs lived included lakes, floodplains, and east-flowing rivers.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the climate was wet and seasonal.
facts.quote: The presence of rapid sedimentation and other evidence suggests a wet, seasonal climate.

facts.statement: Researchers tested its position within the subfamily Centrosaurinae using maximum parsimony and Bayesian phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Lund et al. (2016) tested the position of Machairoceratops within Centrosaurinae by performing maximum parsimony and Bayesian phylogenetic species level analyses.

facts.statement: The maximum parsimony analysis resulted in a large polytomy at the base of Centrosaurinae, resolving only specific subgroups like Centrosaurini and a clade of Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: The maximum parsimony analysis yielded a large polytomy at the base of Centrosaurinae, with only Centrosaurini, most of Pachyrhinosaurini (Einiosaurus, Wendiceratops and Pachyrostra), and a clade formed by Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops being resolved.

facts.statement: In contrast, the Bayesian analysis produced a fully resolved evolutionary tree.
facts.quote: The Bayesian analysis yielded a fully resolved topology which is shown below.

facts.statement: The trace fossil consists of mammalian den complexes and digging grooves likely made by a maniraptoran dinosaur.
facts.quote: The trace fossil includes at least two fossilized mammalian den complexes as well as associated digging grooves presumably caused by a maniraptoran dinosaur.
